short: Malaysia has no AI statute. The National Guidelines on AI Governance and Ethics are voluntary, and no AI bill appears on the Dewan Rakyat's 2026 bill list; the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 binds.
title: Malaysia AI Laws
subtitle: No AI act: voluntary national guidelines and the PDPA
body_html:
Status at a glance

No AI act yet; one in drafting. Malaysia governs AI through the National Guidelines on AI Governance and Ethics (AIGE), published by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation in 2024, which say of themselves that they are voluntary for stakeholders. No AI bill appears on the Dewan Rakyat's list of bills for 2026, updated 21 October 2026. Parliament did pass two related bills that year: the Cybercrimes Bill 2026 (D.R.8/2026, passed 1 July 2026) and the Communications and Multimedia (Amendment) Bill 2026 (D.R.18/2026, passed 15 July 2026). The binding layer for AI processing personal data is the Personal Data Protection Act 2010, amended by Act A1727 in 2024. Verified on 25 October 2026 against MOSTI and the Parliament of Malaysia.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberPublishedLegal force
National Guidelines on AI Governance and EthicsMOSTI2024Voluntary
Personal Data Protection Act 2010Act 709, amended by Act A1727Binding

Who regulates and enforces

  • Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MOSTI): issued the AIGE guidelines.
  • Personal Data Protection Commissioner: enforces the PDPA.

Scope and reach

There is no AI-specific scope. The PDPA applies to the processing of personal data in commercial transactions.

Core obligations

  • No binding AI obligations. The AIGE guidelines set principles for developers, deployers and users, voluntarily.
  • The PDPA's data protection principles bind AI that processes personal data.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Departing from the AIGE guidelinesNone: they are voluntary
PDPA offencesNot stated here: the amended penalties could not be read on an official sourcePDPA 2010, as amended by Act A1727Personal Data Protection Commissioner

What is coming next

No AI bill has been tabled. The Dewan Rakyat's bill list is watched weekly.

The AI Governance Bill in preparation, as reported

An AI act is being drafted, and it is further along than the Dewan Rakyat's bill list shows. Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo told Parliament on 9 February 2026 that his ministry was drafting an AI Governance Bill, to be tabled in 2026, aimed at deepfakes, synthetic content and identity manipulation, with an incident-reporting mechanism and a duty on technology providers to manage risk proactively; he had said on 24 November 2025 that drafting was nearly complete and that a wider legislative framework would go to Cabinet in June 2026. On 10 July 2026 the National AI Office (NAIO) published a consultation paper on the bill with comments to 31 July 2026. As Access Partnership and W.Media summarise it, the bill would apply to every entity in the AI lifecycle, developers and deployers alike, whenever AI is designed, developed or used in Malaysia regardless of where the hardware sits, so foreign platforms reaching Malaysian consumers are in scope; it would set five national AI governance principles (human dignity and agency, proportionate transparency, accountability and redress, safety and resilience, responsible data governance) that developers and deployers apply proportionately; and it would create a Central AI Authority with three functions, AI safety (risk framework, assessments, testing, incident reporting), investigation and enforcement, and ecosystem development. Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said on 21 July 2026 that the bill would be tabled after ministry and agency consultations, using the Online Safety Act process as the model. Access Partnership's indicative timeline runs Cabinet at the end of July 2026, Attorney General's Chambers drafting from August to October, and Parliament in November or December 2026, which is why the October bill list may still be silent.

Around the bill sits a refresh of adjacent law that Gobind listed in November 2025: amendments to the PDPA, the Cyber Security Act 2024 (in operation since 26 August 2024), the Online Safety Act 2025, updates to the Evidence Act 1950 and the Contracts Act 1950, and the Cybercrimes Bill passed in July 2026 to replace the Computer Crimes Act 1997. In February 2026 the minister also described plans for an independent Data Commission to protect national data sovereignty, and CyberSecurity Malaysia was finalising a National Digital Trust and Data Security Strategy 2026 to 2030. The AIGE's seven principles, voluntary today, are the obvious seed for the five in the bill; a company that already documents against them will have most of what the Central AI Authority asks for.

Last verified

4 November 2026, against the sources above. The AI Governance Bill is described from Bernama, the Malaysian press and two consultancy notes, not from the NAIO consultation paper itself, which was not read; the bill's scope, principles and authority are therefore reported, not verified, and may change before tabling. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: the PDPA's penalties as amended in 2024 and its commencement dates, because the PDP portal was under maintenance and the Attorney General's Chambers site refused the request.
